evidence.note: 'Blocking (CPU-bound) code should not be called directly... all concurrent asyncio Tasks and IO operations would be delayed'; use run_in_executor.

'If you are using a third party library that communicates with something (a database, an API...) and doesn't have support for using await... declare your path operation functions as normally, with just def.'
Async use requires AsyncSession/AsyncEngine; the sync Session does blocking IO.

py-sync-client-in-async.whyNotLinter: ruff ASYNC210-251 only know a fixed list (time.sleep, requests/httpx sync, urllib, open, subprocess, input, pathlib). No linter knows which DB drivers, ORM calls and vendor SDK clients are synchronous; this rule deliberately names only those, leaving the literal ASYNC cases to ruff.
py-sync-client-in-async.aiRelevance: High (inferred): agents default FastAPI handlers to `async def` and then use sync SDK/DB clients from examples -- the exact case FastAPI's docs warn about. No direct study found.
py-sync-client-in-async.expectedNoise: low -- the client names make sync vs async visible; residual risk is a custom wrapper whose sync/async nature is not shown.

evidence.note: 'A single instance of AsyncSession is not safe for use in multiple, concurrent tasks'; use a separate AsyncSession per task with asyncio.gather().

py-async-session-shared-concurrently.whyNotLinter: Requires knowing that the shared argument is a session/connection rather than a pool or client; no ruff/mypy rule models object sharing across tasks.
py-async-session-shared-concurrently.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): when asked to speed up sequential awaits (which jev-lint's own gen-sequential-independent-awaits suggests), agents wrap existing `session`-using calls in `gather`. This rule is the safety counterpart.
py-async-session-shared-concurrently.expectedNoise: low -- only fires when a shared session/connection name is passed into concurrent calls.

evidence.note: 'In case asyncio.CancelledError is explicitly caught, it should generally be propagated when clean-up is complete'; TaskGroup and asyncio.timeout() 'might misbehave if a coroutine swallows asyncio.CancelledError'.

py-swallowed-cancellation.whyNotLinter: ruff (0.14) has no port of flake8-async's no-reraise-cancelled; E722/BLE001 flag the catch syntax but not whether cancellation is re-raised in async code, and they are blind to explicit `except CancelledError`.
py-swallowed-cancellation.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): agents write long-running workers with `except asyncio.CancelledError: log; break/return` or catch-all handlers. No direct study.
py-swallowed-cancellation.expectedNoise: low -- the legitimate 'await the task I cancelled' idiom is named in `false`.

evidence.note: API1:2023, the #1 API risk: validate that the logged-in user may access the record the request id names.
Maintainer blog: LLM judges detect missing authorization best when the check is self-contained in the function or absent entirely -- the snippet-visible case this rule targets.
Vendor study of 470 OSS PRs: AI-authored PRs had ~1.7x more issues; performance inefficiencies (excessive I/O, N+1 queries, unindexed lookups) ~8x more often; security issues 1.5-2x.

py-unscoped-object-lookup.whyNotLinter: Authorization is business logic; ruff/bandit have no rule, and CodeQL/Semgrep need app-specific models of the owner field.
py-unscoped-object-lookup.aiRelevance: High: agents generate CRUD endpoints from a model's fields and routinely omit ownership scoping; CodeRabbit (C) reports 1.5-2x more security issues in AI PRs.
py-unscoped-object-lookup.expectedNoise: med -- scoping can live in middleware, a base class, or a `get_queryset` outside the snippet; the `false` list covers the visible cases. Dry-run on real repos before enabling by default.

evidence.note: Warning: when comparing digest()/hexdigest() to an externally supplied digest, use compare_digest() instead of == to reduce vulnerability to timing attacks.

py-secret-compare-eq.whyNotLinter: Needs to know that the operands are secrets; `==` on strings is otherwise fine. No ruff/bandit rule exists for it.
py-secret-compare-eq.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): agents hand-roll webhook signature checks (`if sig != expected:`). No direct study.
py-secret-compare-eq.expectedNoise: low -- operand names (`signature`, `expected_digest`, `api_key`) make intent visible.

evidence.note: on_commit() is for background tasks, email notifications and cache invalidation that must happen only if the transaction commits.

py-side-effect-in-transaction.whyNotLinter: Requires recognising external side effects and transaction scope together; no ruff/Django check exists.
py-side-effect-in-transaction.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): agents add `.delay(obj.id)` right after `obj.save()` wherever the save is, including inside `atomic`.
py-side-effect-in-transaction.expectedNoise: low -- both the transaction block and the side-effect call must be visible.

evidence.note: 'Avoiding race conditions using F()': a thread can retrieve, increment and save after another retrieved it; 'the work of the first thread will be lost'.
Use F expressions / QuerySet.update() rather than retrieve-set-save.

py-read-modify-write-race.whyNotLinter: Needs to recognise that a numeric field is shared persistent state and that no lock/atomic update is used; no static rule does this.
py-read-modify-write-race.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): inventory, credit and balance code written by agents is typically naive read-modify-write.
py-read-modify-write-race.expectedNoise: low-med -- counters on freshly created objects are excluded by `false`.

evidence.note: 'You should only ever use the model_construct() method with data which has already been validated, or that you definitely trust'; V2 made its performance advantage much smaller.

py-pydantic-construct-bypass.whyNotLinter: Whether the input is trusted is a data-provenance judgment; a ban on `model_construct` would hit legitimate trusted uses.
py-pydantic-construct-bypass.aiRelevance: Low-medium: agents reach for `model_construct` to silence validation errors. Rare but high impact.
py-pydantic-construct-bypass.expectedNoise: low -- fires only on `construct(` with visibly external data.
